description: Native DeepAgents Skills Support - Thread skills parameter through agent construction chain and merge Assistant.files into ToolRuntime state for progressive skill loading

userStories.title: Add `skills` field to Assistant and LLMRequest schemas
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Assistant and LLMRequest models to accept a skills field so users can configure skill directory paths and they flow through the request chain.
acceptanceCriteria: Assistant model in backend/src/schemas/entities/llm.py has a new `skills: Optional[List[str]]` field with `default_factory=list`
Field description reads: 'Skill directory paths for progressive loading (e.g., ["./skills/"])'
LLMRequest model in backend/src/schemas/entities/llm.py has a new `skills: Optional[List[str]]` field with `default_factory=list`
skills field is placed after the subagents field in LLMRequest
Assistant.to_llm_request() passes `skills=self.skills` to the returned LLMRequest
Existing assistants without skills default to empty list (no behavior change)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Both schema changes are in the same file (backend/src/schemas/entities/llm.py). Follow the exact pattern used by the `subagents` field. The `to_llm_request()` method already passes subagents — add skills in the same fashion.

userStories.title: Thread `skills` through `init_graph()` to `create_deep_agent()`
userStories.description: As a developer, I need init_graph() to accept and forward a skills parameter so that create_deep_agent() receives it and activates progressive skill loading.
acceptanceCriteria: init_graph() in backend/src/agents/__init__.py accepts `skills: list[str] | None = None` parameter
skills is passed to create_deep_agent(skills=skills) call inside init_graph()
When skills=None, create_deep_agent() does not activate skill loading (existing behavior preserved)
When skills=['./skills/'], the agent is configured to look for skills in that directory
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow the same pattern as the `subagents` parameter in init_graph(). The create_deep_agent() function from deepagents==0.3.8 already accepts `skills: list[str] | None = None` as a keyword argument.

userStories.title: Thread `skills` through `Orchestra.__init__()` and `construct_agent()`
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Orchestra class and construct_agent() to accept and forward a skills parameter to init_graph().
acceptanceCriteria: Orchestra.__init__() in backend/src/agents/__init__.py accepts `skills: list[str] | None = None` parameter
Orchestra stores skills as self.skills instance variable
Orchestra passes skills=self.skills to init_graph() in the deepagent graph_id branch
construct_agent() in backend/src/agents/__init__.py accepts `skills: list[str] | None = None` parameter
construct_agent() passes skills=skills to Orchestra() constructor
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Both Orchestra.__init__() and construct_agent() are in the same file (backend/src/agents/__init__.py). Follow the exact pattern used by the subagents parameter in both functions.

userStories.title: Thread `skills` and merge Assistant.files in streaming entry point
userStories.description: As an end user chatting via the streaming API, I want the agent to have access to skill files stored in my assistant configuration so it can progressively load relevant skills during conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: stream_generator() in backend/src/utils/stream.py accepts `files: dict | None = None` and `skills: list[str] | None = None` parameters
Assistant-level files are merged into files_map: `files_map = {**(files or {}), **(config['metadata'].get('files', {}) or input.files or {})}`
skills is passed to construct_agent() via the skills kwarg
llm_stream() in backend/src/controllers/llm.py passes assistant.skills and assistant.files to stream_generator()
Agent works normally when no skills are configured
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Two files modified: stream.py (add parameters and merge files) and controllers/llm.py (pass assistant.skills and assistant.files). The file merge order is: assistant files as base, request files override. Pattern: {**assistant.files, **request.files}.

userStories.title: Pass `skills` and merge Assistant.files in direct invoke entry point
userStories.description: As an API consumer using the direct invoke endpoint, I want the agent to have access to skills for consistent behavior across invoke and stream paths.
acceptanceCriteria: llm_invoke() in backend/src/controllers/llm.py merges assistant files into params.input.files before init_backend()
File merge follows same pattern as streaming: assistant files as base, request files override
skills is passed to construct_agent() via the skills kwarg
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Only backend/src/controllers/llm.py is modified. The llm_invoke() function already calls construct_agent() — add skills=params.skills to that call. Also merge assistant.files into params.input.files before the init_backend() call.

userStories.title: Thread `skills` and merge files in worker entry point
userStories.description: As an end user with distributed agent tasks, I want those background agents to also have access to skills for consistent behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: _execute_agent_stream() in backend/src/workers/tasks.py passes skills=params.skills to construct_agent()
Assistant files are merged into files_map in the worker path following the same merge pattern as streaming
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Only backend/src/workers/tasks.py is modified. Follow the same pattern as the subagents parameter already passed to construct_agent() in this function.

userStories.title: Run backend tests and validate no regressions
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to confirm all existing tests pass with no regressions after threading the skills parameter through the agent construction chain.
acceptanceCriteria: Run `make test` and all existing tests pass
Run `make format` and all files pass lint/typecheck
No behavior change for existing assistants without skills configured
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is a validation-only story. Run the full test suite and format checks. Fix any regressions found.

userStories.title: Validate frontend loads and assistant creation still works via agent-browser
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to verify the frontend still functions correctly after the backend schema changes, ensuring assistant creation, editing, and chat streaming are not broken by the new skills field.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Navigate to the app login page (http://localhost:5173) and confirm it loads without errors
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Log in with test credentials and confirm successful authentication redirect to the main chat interface

Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Navigate to assistant creation/settings page and confirm the form renders correctly — existing fields (name, description, model, system_prompt, tools) are all visible and functional
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Create a new assistant WITHOUT skills configured — confirm it saves successfully and appears in the assistant list, verifying backward compatibility

Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Open an existing assistant and confirm its configuration loads correctly with no console errors — the new skills field with empty default should not break existing assistant loading
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Start a new chat with an existing assistant — type a test message, send it, and confirm streaming response renders correctly in the chat UI with no errors

Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: Open browser developer tools console and confirm there are no JavaScript errors or failed API requests (4xx/5xx) related to the assistant or chat endpoints

Verify in browser using agent-browser skill: If an assistant edit/update form exists, update an existing assistant's name or description and confirm the save operation completes without errors — the new skills field should serialize correctly in the API payload
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This story requires the dev server running (make dev for backend, npm run dev for frontend). Use the agent-browser skill to perform each validation step. The key concern is that adding the `skills` field to the Assistant schema could cause frontend deserialization issues if the frontend TypeScript types are tightly coupled to the API response shape. Check for TypeScript strict mode errors and API response handling.
